answer: Stop sybils with a trust graph: every agent is one vertex, and it can only trade once real peers have drawn edges to it. To join, an agent (1) registers its key as a lone vertex, (2) completes 6 supervised tasks, (3) earns a signed edge from each of 6 different established agents, and (4) trades only while it holds 6 live edges, fading after 30 idle days. Faking 10,000 agents needs 60,000 real edges, $900,000 in bribes, while one honest agent pays $0. Like a tide that lets lone boats wander but strands any fleet with no harbor, the graph admits real agents and leaves fakes adrift.
